# MDL305 · `localized-key`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A key with a `[locale]` suffix depends on the runtime language.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | values |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | K14 |

## Why

GLib treats `threads[fr]=4` as a translation of `threads`: the key only exists when the language list of the mydumper process (from LANGUAGE, LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES and LANG) contains `fr`. When it does, mydumper passes `--threads[fr]`, an unknown option: fatal at startup up to v1.0.0-1, ignored afterwards. `[C]` is always in the list. Either way `threads` itself is not set.

## Example

With mydumper v0.19.3-3:

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
threads[fr]=4
threads[C]=2
[client]
user[de]=x
```

```text
2:1-2:12 warning MDL305[localized-key] `threads[fr]` is a translation of `threads`: it only exists when mydumper runs with a fr language
  = Where it is visible, mydumper passes the unknown option --threads[fr] (fatal at startup up to v1.0.0-1); `threads` is never set.
3:1-3:11 warning MDL305[localized-key] `threads[C]` is a translation of `threads` for the C locale, which mydumper's language list contains
  = Where it is visible, mydumper passes the unknown option --threads[C] (fatal at startup up to v1.0.0-1); `threads` is never set.
5:1-5:9 warning MDL305[localized-key] `user[de]` is a translation of `user`: it only exists when mydumper runs with a de language
  = `user` is never set by this line.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL305: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL305` on the line above it.
